title: Legalisation of Local Liquor Could Help Curb Illicit Sale, Says Former Manipur CM N. Biren Singh
summary: Former Manipur Chief Minister N. Biren Singh says regulating and legalising locally brewed liquor could help curb illicit sales, while urging unity amid the state's ongoing crisis.
body:
Imphal, November 22, 2026: Former Manipur Chief Minister Nongthombam Biren Singh has said that legalising locally brewed liquor could help regulate its sale and curb the illegal liquor trade. However, he cautioned that such a move could also produce unintended consequences if it was not implemented carefully.

Biren made the remarks while speaking at the inauguration of the Judo Hall (Dojo) of Marjing Judo Academy at Heingang Mayai Leikai. The programme was attended by Youth Affairs and Sports Director, Home Department Joint Secretary Mayengbam Veto, Handlooms and Textiles Director and Registrar of Cooperative Societies W. Ibohal, among others.

Speaking at the event, Biren said he had long supported the idea of regulating locally brewed liquor. Recalling earlier efforts to explore its legalisation, he said experts from Goa had been invited to conduct a survey on the matter. However, the initiative reportedly encountered considerable opposition.

His remarks come amid renewed public attention on the regulation of liquor following the recent suspected spurious liquor tragedy in Manipur. The question of how locally produced liquor is regulated, monitored and sold has become particularly significant in discussions about preventing illicit trade and protecting public health.

Turning to the prevailing political situation in the state, Biren said several efforts had been made to resolve the ongoing crisis. He stressed that people should stand together and avoid confrontation among themselves, calling for unity at a critical time for Manipur.

Referring to the 1979 incident at Waichong, Biren alleged that a decision had been taken during a Kuki gathering to pursue the creation of a separate homeland. He further claimed that Kuki groups were preparing to organise campaigns seeking a separate administration in different Indian cities between December 1 and 12. These remarks represent his allegations and have not been independently established in the information provided.

Biren also criticised what he described as inconsistent political positions on the National Register of Citizens (NRC). He said political leaders should consider the long-term interests of future generations instead of using sensitive issues for electoral advantage.

"Politics should be guided by the future of our generations. While building roads, community halls and clubs, we must also understand where we stand and what we are working towards," he said.

Emphasising collective responsibility, Biren said Manipur was passing through a critical period and warned that continued divisions and a lack of cooperation could lead to further suffering. He urged people to remain united, engage in dialogue and work collectively to address the challenges facing the state.

His remarks brought together two significant concerns facing Manipur: the need for effective regulation of locally brewed liquor and the broader demand for unity and dialogue amid the state's continuing political and social challenges.
author: Mirror Lilong Desk
